title: Integral Apollonian Curvatures: Integrality ⟺ Square Discriminant
description: The integrality phenomenon behind integral Apollonian gaskets. Working with the integer Descartes relation (a+b+c+d)² = 2(a²+b²+c²+d²): the conjugate Soddy curvature soddyReflect a b c d = 2(a+b+c)−d is again an integer Descartes solution, so integer curvatures propagate through the gasket (descartesRelZ_reflect). The headline exists_integral_fourth_iff_sq shows an integer fourth curvature completing a,b,c exists IFF the symmetric product ab+bc+ca is a perfect square — the discriminant dictionary for integral base quadruples. A cast bridge ties this to the parent's real-valued descartesRel, yielding apollonian_new_curvature_isInt: from integer real curvatures satisfying Descartes, the reflected Soddy curvature is again an integer.

Scope: the arithmetic of integral Apollonian gaskets — integrality propagation under Soddy reflection and the perfect-square discriminant characterization of integer base quadruples. It does NOT construct the geometric gasket (nested tangency configuration) nor prove every reachable curvature is enumerated; the single-step reflection closure plus the existence dictionary are what is formalized.

overview.historicalContext: Descartes' 1643 curvature relation for four mutually tangent circles underlies the theory of Apollonian circle packings. When a base quadruple of mutually tangent circles has integer curvatures, repeatedly inscribing the Soddy circle tangent to three of them produces an infinite packing in which EVERY curvature is an integer — an integral Apollonian gasket. The arithmetic structure of these gaskets (studied by Graham, Lagarias, Mallows, Wilks, and Yan, building on the 2002 complex Descartes theorem) is a rich source of number theory, including local-global conjectures on which integers appear as curvatures. The engine of integrality is elementary: by Vieta, the two solutions of the Descartes quadratic in the fourth curvature sum to twice the sum of the other three, so each new curvature 2(k₁+k₂+k₃)−k₄ is an integer combination of integers.
overview.problemStatement: Give a clean Lean statement of the integrality phenomenon for the Descartes Circle Theorem: integer curvatures propagating through the Apollonian gasket, and the discriminant condition (the symmetric product a·b + b·c + c·a being a perfect square) governing when an integer base quadruple exists.
overview.proofStrategy: Everything is driven by one completing-the-square identity. Viewing the Descartes relation as a quadratic in the fourth curvature d, `descartesRelZ_iff_sq` rewrites it as the discriminant identity (d−(a+b+c))² = 4(ab+bc+ca); both directions are a single `linear_combination`. From this, three threads run in parallel: (1) the conjugate root soddyReflect = 2(a+b+c)−d is read off by Vieta, is subtraction-only (hence integer-preserving), and the reflection theorem `descartesRelZ_reflect` is a pure ring identity giving closure of integer quadruples under reflection; (2) the headline biconditional extracts a perfect square — the forward direction is the only place arithmetic beyond `ring` enters, using primality of 2 (`Int.prime_two`, `Prime.dvd_of_dvd_pow`) to pass from 4 ∣ (d−(a+b+c))² to 2 ∣ (d−(a+b+c)), then cancelling 4; the reverse direction is the explicit witness d = (a+b+c)+2m; (3) a `push_cast`/`exact_mod_cast` bridge (`descartesRelZ_iff_real`) reuses the integer reflection theorem to make the capstone statement about real curvatures that happen to be integers.
keyInsights: Completing the square in the fourth curvature converts the symmetric Descartes relation into the discriminant identity (d−(a+b+c))² = 4(ab+bc+ca); the symmetric product ab+bc+ca is the discriminant that controls everything else.

Integrality propagates for free: by Vieta the conjugate Soddy curvature is 2(a+b+c)−d, a purely additive expression, so no square root ever appears and the new curvature is automatically an integer — this is the entire reason integral Apollonian gaskets stay integral.

The reflection closure `descartesRelZ_reflect` is a ring identity valid over any commutative ring; positivity, ordering, and the reals are never needed for the propagation step — only for the geometric interpretation.

Primality of 2 is the lone non-formal arithmetic input: 4 ∣ (d−(a+b+c))² gives 2 ∣ (d−(a+b+c)) precisely because 2 is prime, which is what forces the half-difference to be an integer and the discriminant to be an exact square.
The involution soddyReflect ∘ soddyReflect = id is the ℤ₂ generator behind the Apollonian group; the full gasket is the orbit of one base quadruple under the four such reflections.
keyResults: Integer curvatures propagate: the Soddy reflection 2(a+b+c)−d of an integer Descartes quadruple is again an integer Descartes quadruple.
An integer fourth curvature completing a,b,c exists if and only if a·b + b·c + c·a is a perfect square.
Real phrasing: starting from integer curvatures satisfying the parent's real Descartes relation, the reflected Soddy curvature is again an integer.

sections.title: The Integer Descartes Relation and Discriminant Identity
sections.summary: Defines `descartesRelZ`, the curvature relation over ℤ, and proves `descartesRelZ_iff_sq`: completing the square in d rewrites the relation as (d−(a+b+c))² = 4(ab+bc+ca). This discriminant identity is the engine for everything below.

sections.title: Conjugate Soddy Curvature and Its Involution
sections.summary: Defines `soddyReflect a b c d = 2(a+b+c)−d`, the second root of the Descartes quadratic, and proves `soddyReflect_involutive` — reflecting twice returns the original (the ℤ₂ swap between the two Soddy circles).

sections.title: Gasket-Generation Step and Vieta Relations
sections.summary: `descartesRelZ_reflect` shows the conjugate of an integer Descartes quadruple is again one (integrality propagates), and `soddy_sum_Z` / `soddy_prod_Z` give the Vieta sum 2(a+b+c) and product (a+b+c)²−4(ab+bc+ca) of the two completing curvatures.

sections.title: Existence Dictionary: Integrality ⟺ Square Discriminant
sections.summary: `exists_integral_fourth_iff_sq`: an integer fourth curvature completing a,b,c exists iff ab+bc+ca is a perfect square. The forward direction uses primality of 2 to force 2 ∣ (d−(a+b+c)); the reverse exhibits d = (a+b+c)+2m.

sections.title: Cast Bridge and Real-Curvature Integrality
sections.summary: `descartesRelZ_iff_real` bridges the integer relation to the parent's real `descartesRel` via `exact_mod_cast`, and `apollonian_new_curvature_isInt` transports the reflection theorem back to real curvatures: integer real curvatures satisfying Descartes reflect to another integer curvature.

conclusion.summary: This leaf formalizes the arithmetic backbone of integral Apollonian gaskets. From a single completing-the-square identity it derives that integer Descartes quadruples are closed under Soddy reflection (so an integral packing stays integral as circles are inscribed), the Vieta relations for the two completing curvatures, and the headline existence dictionary: three integer curvatures extend to an integer quadruple exactly when their symmetric product ab+bc+ca is a perfect square. A cast bridge transports the propagation statement to the parent's real-valued Descartes relation. All results are fully machine-checked with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The reflection-closure result is the formal justification for why integral Apollonian gaskets exist at all: integrality is preserved by the Apollonian group's generators because each generator is the subtraction-only map d ↦ 2(a+b+c)−d, with no square roots to leave ℤ. The perfect-square discriminant criterion is a concrete diophantine test for when an integer base quadruple can be assembled, connecting the geometry to classical number theory (sums and products of integers that are squares). These are exactly the structures studied in the local–global theory of curvatures in Apollonian packings (Graham–Lagarias–Mallows–Wilks–Yan).
openQuestions: Which integers actually occur as curvatures in a given integral gasket? The Apollonian local–global conjecture predicts that all sufficiently large integers in the admissible congruence classes appear — formalizing even the statement would extend this entry substantially.

Can the single-step reflection closure be iterated in Lean to construct the full Apollonian orbit as a generated subgroup/sub-set, certifying that every reachable curvature is an integer rather than only one reflection step?

Is there a clean Lean characterization of *primitive* integer quadruples (gcd of the four curvatures equal to 1), and of the root quadruple minimizing the curvatures, mirroring the reduction theory used in the arithmetic of gaskets?
